title: Towing and Labor Coverage and the Owner Term: Termination, Restoration, Expiration and Removal
content:
**Towing and Labor Coverage** follows the owner term it is attached to: it ends, is restored and expires with the owner term. The towing coverage is terminated only when its owner term has been cancelled. It is restored when the owner term is reinstated and expires with it. A removal takes effect on the date requested, never earlier. These terms are the same on every Cardinal Point Towing and Labor package ($50 through $200).

## Termination

Termination rests on the company's record of the owner term the coverage is attached to: the coverage is terminated only when that owner term's status is cancelled, judged before the termination is booked.

| Status of the owner term on the company's records | The towing coverage may be terminated |
|---|---|
| Cancelled | Yes |
| Any other status | No |

## Coverage statuses and what moves them

| From | To | What brings it about |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled | Active | The effective date is reached (by the system) |
| Scheduled | Removed | The named insured removes it before it starts |
| Active | Removed | The named insured removes it |
| Active | Terminated | The owner term is cancelled |
| Terminated | Active | The owner term is reinstated (the coverage is restored) |
| Active | Expired | The owner term expires (by the system) |

## Removal

A removal is made at the named insured's request, while the coverage is scheduled or active, and takes effect on the date requested, never earlier.

*Hypothetical:* the named insured asks for the coverage to be removed as of the 20th of a month; the removal takes effect on the 20th, not on any earlier day.

## Points of judgement

- **Ending the coverage while the owner term continues.** Termination belongs only to a cancelled owner term. A coverage that ends at the named insured's request while the owner term remains open ends by removal.
- **Reinstatement.** A coverage that was terminated because its owner term was cancelled becomes active again when that owner term is reinstated.
- **Expiration.** An active coverage expires when its owner term expires; it does not run beyond the owner term.
